lines: Imagine falling from the sky through a violent storm and waking up alone in a deadly jungle.
On 24 December 1971 a passenger plane is struck by lightning and breaks apart midair.
Seventeen year old Juliane Koepcke falls about 3000 meters while still strapped to her seat row.
She wakes up on the dark forest floor with a broken collarbone and a deep arm cut.
She also suffers from a painful eye injury and a severe concussion after the terrifying plunge.
Her biologist father previously taught her that following flowing water always leads back to people.
She finds a tiny creek and begins walking through the dense and dangerous Peruvian rainforest.
Days pass slowly as she follows the winding water toward a larger and safer river.
Up to 14 other passengers survive the initial crash but tragically die before any rescue arrives.
She spends 11 long days completely alone in the unforgiving jungle facing unimaginable odds.
After 9 days of difficult travel she finally discovers a remote lumberjack camp by the river.
She is found by local workers who provide medical help and bring her back to safety.
Juliane remains the only official survivor of LANSA Flight 508 against all odds and expectations.
Would you have the mental strength to survive 11 days alone in the dangerous rainforest?
draft_evening.title: The Girl Who Fell 3000 Meters And Survived
draft_evening.description: Seventeen year old Juliane Koepcke falls from the sky into the Peruvian rainforest and survives alone for 11 days.

lines: If lightning strikes on a mountain peak, do not seek shelter under a lone tree.
Jake is hiking above the tree line at dusk when dark clouds fill the sky.
He has less than 5 minutes before a deadly thunderstorm hits his open position.
A huge lightning bolt flashes nearby with a roaring crash of loud thunder.
When thunder roars, go indoors because no place outside is ever truly safe.
Only a sturdy building or a hard-top car offers real protection from lightning strikes.
One. Get off peaks and high ridges immediately and start heading down right away.
Jake starts to run away down the steep mountain slope, leaving the high peak.
Two. Never shelter under a lone tree or stand near dangerous metal fences.
Jake avoids a single pine tree and keeps moving quickly to lower ground.
Three. Spread a group out so 1 strike does not hit everyone at once.
Jake sees a solid rock overhang down the slope and moves toward it quickly.
He reaches the ledge and moves inside to enter shelter from the storm.
Jake did everything right to survive the sudden storm on the mountain peak.
It was the perfect plan, but there was just 1 big problem waiting inside.
Freezing rainwater floods the shelter while dusk fades into absolute darkness around Jake.
part1.cliffhanger: Freezing runoff water floods Jake's rock shelter just as total darkness sets in on the mountain.
